Repo: /opt/nxeon-v2, branch design/v2 — a from-scratch visual redesign ("Nexion") of the real Nxeon hosting platform, running sandboxed (NXEON_SANDBOX=1: real DB and code paths, no VM ever provisions, no card ever charges). Read /opt/nxeon-v2/CLAUDE.md FIRST for the operating rules (never build in /opt/nxeon, never pkill -f by pattern, verification-by-screenshot discipline, etc). Login: customer@nxeon.local / wGPZqhCbsLdz (see /root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt), base URL https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud.

CONTEXT — a long session just finished building a light theme for this whole dashboard (dark was the only mode before; light is new, toggled via `data-theme="light"` on `<html>`, tokens as `--color-*` CSS custom properties in app/globals.css) and found/fixed a long tail of bugs across most pages. You are ONE of 4 parallel agents auditing the REMAINING, not-yet-checked pages for the same classes of bugs. COORDINATION: you may rebuild (./rebuild.sh) and restart the nxeon-v2-web service as needed for your own verification — just don't leave it down when you finish, and do NOT create git commits (the orchestrating session commits everyone's work together). Stay within your assigned pages/files (listed below) so you don't collide with the other 3 agents working the same tree concurrently.

YOUR PAGES: /dashboard/mail (a full webmail app — inbox, compose, settings, likely several sub-views under components/customer/mail/*, this is probably your biggest page), /dashboard/email (business email hosting, distinct from mail), /dashboard/calendar, /dashboard/order, /dashboard/claude-code. Also glance at /dashboard/build (the Matrix AI-build console, components/nx/MatrixPanel.tsx) — it was ALREADY fixed for its hero this session, but check the actual build/console workspace UI underneath the hero (components/customer/claude-code/BuildStudio.tsx and friends) since that inner workspace was NOT part of the earlier fix. Find each page's component via app/dashboard/<name>/page.tsx and grep from there.

THE BUG TAXONOMY TO CHECK FOR ON EVERY PAGE (all of these have been found and fixed repeatedly elsewhere this session — you're checking whether the same mistakes exist on your assigned pages):
1. A literal hardcoded color (hex or rgba, e.g. `bg-[rgba(10,22,48,.5)]`, `text-[#7f9ad0]`) used for something that should adapt between themes, instead of the theme's own `--color-*` tokens / `text-tx`, `text-tx-dim`, `text-tx-faint`, `border-rim-hi`, `bg-well`, `bg-surface`, `.card`/`.card-glass`, etc. (grep app/globals.css for the full token list). On the light page these often render as either invisible-on-invisible or a jarring leftover dark box.
2. A hero/banner section with its own fixed dark background + `text-white` heading — if it's not wrapped in the `.nx-dark-island` CSS class (also in app/globals.css), light mode's generic fix flips `text-white` to dark ink, making it invisible against a scrim that stayed dark on purpose. Look for `<header>` or hero `<div>`s with a literal dark gradient background.
3. `bg-white` (bare, not `bg-white/NN`) used to mean "always paint this literally white" (e.g. a toggle switch knob, an active-segment pill) — this breaks because `--color-white` now means "ink" in light mode. Fix: literal `bg-[#fff]` if it must always be bright regardless of theme, or a proper light-mode-aware treatment otherwise.
4. An `Icon` component (components/nx/Icon.tsx) rendered with no `tone` prop inside a colored/gradient badge that has an intended contrasting text color set on the wrapper — the icon overrides that intended color with its own default tone class instead of inheriting it. Fix: pass `tone="inherit"`.
5. `text-white/NN` (opacity-modified) sitting on something that is NOT actually a light-mode-adapted surface (e.g. its own literal-color decorative card) — gets wrongly retargeted by the global opacity-decoupling rule meant for text sitting on the actual page background.
6. Any canvas/backdrop using `globalCompositeOperation = "lighter"` or CSS `mix-blend-screen`/`mix-blend-lighten` — these only ever add light and wash to grey on a light page. If you find one NOT already using components/nx/auroraTheme.ts's `isLightTheme()`/`auroraComposite()`/`auroraStrandGradient()` helpers, wire it in (read components/nx/DomainsAurora.tsx as a working example of the pattern) rather than reinventing the fix.
7. A `.card-on`-style "selected" state, or any custom selected/active-state styling, that renders as a solid dark block regardless of theme — should look intentional (accent border/glow) rather than like a hole punched in an otherwise light page.
8. Genuine FUNCTIONAL bugs unrelated to theming — broken layout, a button that does nothing, a modal that doesn't close, text that's cut off, a state that never updates. Mail especially: check the reading pane, compose window, and attachment/image lightbox (components/ui/LightboxImage.tsx was just fixed to portal to document.body — if mail uses its own separate lightbox/attachment-preview implementation instead of that shared component, check it for the same "trapped inside a backdrop-filter ancestor" bug).

WORKFLOW: for each page, log in via a Playwright script (must live under /opt/nxeon-v2/scripts/ per CLAUDE.md, e.g. scripts/_audit_c.mjs — delete it when you're done, this repo's convention is not to leave one-off scripts lying around), screenshot in BOTH dark (default) and light mode (`localStorage.setItem('nx-theme','light'); document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme','light')` before navigating, same trick used everywhere else this session), actually LOOK at the screenshots (read them back as images), diagnose anything that looks wrong using the taxonomy above, fix it in the source, rebuild, re-screenshot to confirm the fix, then move to the next page. Run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` after every batch of edits.

Don't invent problems that aren't there — several pages may already be fine (if a page already uses `.card`/`.card-glass`/tokens throughout, it likely needs nothing). Only fix what's actually visibly or functionally broken. Write a final report listing every bug found (with a short description and the file it was in) and every fix made, plus any page you found to already be correct.

content.content: # Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong: ```bash scripts/node1.sh cards "dashboard" # find concept cards by title scripts/node1.sh board # list that card's attachments scripts/node1.sh pull # copy them to /tmp/board/ scripts/node1.sh db "select …" # read-only query against PROD scripts/node1.sh sh '' # anything else ``` **That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production database and the mail server. Treat it as read-only.** Never write to the prod DB (the `db` subcommand refuses obvious writes, which is a guard against a slip, not a security boundary), never edit `/opt/nxeon`, never build there, never restart a prod service. If you genuinely need to change something on node-1, **stop and ask the owner first.** ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run builds in `/opt/nxeon`.** That is live production; clobbering its `.next` has taken the admin panel down before. 3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"` restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit. 4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink. 5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and before spending on any paid third-party tool. 6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off. 7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone. 8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file. ## Verification discipline A change is not done until it is **deployed and screenshotted**.
